run.procedureSummary:
Every cycle runs the five steps below in order, and each step finishes on all six crucibles before the next one starts.
1. Charge: add the cycle's row to crucibles 1 to 6. Volume is ignored at this step.
2. Overflow: go through crucibles 1 to 6 one at a time. Any amount over a crucible's working volume moves to the next crucible before that crucible is checked, so overflow can cascade along the line. Overflow from crucible 6 goes to slag.
3. State: judge each crucible on its post-overflow quantity only. A BASE crucible at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. A SUPERHEATED crucible at or below its lower mark becomes BASE. Anything else stays as it is.
4. Return: first work out every crucible's amount from the post-overflow quantity and the state just set, rounding down. A BASE crucible gives a quarter of its contents to slag. A SUPERHEATED crucible gives half of its contents to the crucible on its charging side, and crucible 1's half goes to slag. All amounts then move at the same moment. Overfill stays where it is until the next cycle's overflow step, and nothing is done about it after cycle 5.
5. Emergency tap: if total melt after the return is strictly above 38, every crucible keeps half its contents, rounded down, and the rest goes to slag.
I used a short Python script for the arithmetic (C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\sim.py) and then re-derived every cycle by hand; the hand figures match the script.

openPoints.point: Where overflow from a full crucible goes when the next crucible is also over volume
openPoints.assumption: The excess is added to the next crucible before that crucible is checked, so it can carry on down the line (for example cycle 4 runs 1 to 2 to 3 to 4 to 5 to 6 to slag).

openPoints.point: Which state the return step uses
openPoints.assumption: The state set in step 3 of the same cycle, applied to the quantities after overflow.

openPoints.point: When the tap's 38 test is made, and what counts as firing
openPoints.assumption: Total melt is checked after the return step, and the tap fires only when the total is strictly above 38. Cycle 5 ends at exactly 38, so the tap did not fire there.
Every quarter and half is rounded down for each crucible separately. For the tap, each crucible keeps half its contents rounded down, and the rest (the remainder included) goes to slag.

openPoints.point: Over-volume contents left at the end of cycle 5
openPoints.assumption: The end figures are reported as they stand: crucible 2 holds 10 against a working volume of 8, and nothing is moved after cycle 5.

openPoints.point: Whether the state is re-checked after the return or the tap
openPoints.assumption: No. The state changes only in step 3, so the end states are the ones set in cycle 5's step 3.
